{{For|keywords such as {{st|Reload}} and {{st|Holy Shield}}|Keywords}}
{{For|elements such as {{el|Fire}}|Elements}}

In Mewgenics, units can suffer a variety of different '''Status Effects'''. These can be positive buff, negative debuffs or neutral.

Stat Up and Stat Down buffs are actually the same buff, simply having a different visual depending on if the unit has a positive or negative amount.
* As an example: {{st|All Stats Down|#=2}} + {{st|All Stats Up|#=+2}} would result in 0, and no status effect remaining.
** The unit cannot be cleansed afterwards to get back the +2 All Stats Up, because they don't have it anymore.
* But temporary and regular ones are 2 seperate buffs, and will not directly deduce each other.
** {{st|Damage Down|#=Temporary 2}} + {{st|Damage Up|#=2}}, the damage down can be cleansed because it is a seperate status effect.
* Effects that last while a condition is active, such as {{d|Depression}}, will not subtract from either version. <!--Aura stuff-->
** {{st|All Stats Up|#=+2}} shows 0 while next to a cat with Depression, but will return after it moves.
<!--secret 4th thing brittle stats-->

Some status effects cannot be stacked by being applied multiple times. In cases where a higher amount would be applied, it will apply it.
* {{st|Stun|#=1}} on a unit with {{st|Stun|#=1}} = {{st|Stun|#=1}}
* {{st|Stun|#=2}} on a unit with {{st|Stun|#=1}} = {{st|Stun|#=2}}

Downed units have almost all their status effects removed. 
* Some remain as indicators and some are simply inactive, but most are cleared.

Passive effects which give status effects do not reapply them if revived mid battle.

== Buffs ==
Buffs can be removed by [[List_of_effects_that_remove_status_effects#Buffs|purging]] effects, of which there are few.

{{Status Effects Table|Buff}}

== Debuffs ==
Debuffs can be removed by [[List_of_effects_that_remove_status_effects#Debuffs|cleansing]] effects.

{{Status Effects Table|Debuff}}

== Neutral ==
Neutral Status Effects cannot be removed by cleansing effects.

{{Status Effects Table|Neutral}}

* All Elite Buffs and enemy specific buffs below are also neutral.

== Elite Effects ==
{{main|Elites}}
These are unique effects exclusive to {{icon|Elite|link=y}} enemies that change their color and give them unique properties that make them more challenging to fight. They are technically separate from other Status Effects, meaning they cannot be removed. 
* Enemies that are spawned by {{icon|Elite}} enemies generally inherit their summoners Elite effects.
* Various enemies are "blacklisted" from spawning with certain Elite effects, often to prevent unfair scenarios with nigh-unkillable enemies or because it would break the enemy's design. For example, an {{icon|Elite}} {{en|Love Bot}} cannot gain {{st|Elite Buff: Mad}} since it would have no allies to support and heal. 
** All [[familiars]] are banned from getting {{st|Elite Buff: Mad}} to stop them from hurting their allies.
* Elite buffs which give status effects can effectively be nullified by having those status effects removed with something like {{a|Bloodletting}}, such as {{st|Elite Buff: Damaging}} or {{st|Elite Buff: Speedy}}.
* Some Elite buffs have slightly different effects depending on if they are on a standard enemy or a miniboss/boss.

{{:StatusEffects/Elite}}

== Trivia ==
Several status effects appear to be based on similar status effects from other Rpgs. These include:
=== Pokémon ===
* {{st|Burn}}: The victim takes damage each turn, though the timing of the damage in ''Pokémon'' is more similar to {{St|Bleed}} (at the end of a round of turns). Burn in ''Mewgenics'' does ''not'' decrease the afflicted unit's physical attack power, unlike in ''Pokémon''.
* {{st|Freeze}}: The victim is frozen and can't perform actions until it thaws over time. Damaging a frozen target with {{el|Fire}} damage thaws them early. Cannot be frozen when there is {{st|Heat Wave|harsh sunlight}} present. The invulnerability while frozen is also in older ''[[bulba:Pokemon Mystery Dungeon series|Pokemon Mystery Dungeon]]'' games.
* {{st|Poison}}: The victim takes damage each turn, though the timing of the damage in ''Pokémon'' is more similar to {{St|Bleed}} (at the end of a round of turns).
* {{st|Sleep}}: The victim is asleep and cannot perform actions, will wake up after a period of time.
** {{st|Drowsy}}: The victim falls asleep at the end of a turn.
* {{st|Confusion}}: The victim has a random chance to cancel an attack and instead hit themselves.
* {{st|Leeches}}: Resembles [[bulba:Seeding|Leech Seed]]. The victim loses health at the end of a turn, and the one who inflicted that status heals for that amount.
* {{st|Flying}}: Similar to the passive effects of [[bulba:Flying (type)|Flying type]] Pokémon, such as immunity to effects on the ground.

=== Magic: The Gathering ===
* {{st|Lifesteal}}: Resembles the "lifelink" keyword. Dealing damage heals the attacker an amount equal to the damage dealt.
* {{st|Trample}}: Shares a name with the "trample" keyword but is otherwise mechanically very different. Still carries the flavor of a large creature stomping past/ignoring a smaller creature (while crushing the smaller creature in the process).

=== Dungeons & Dragons ===
* {{st|Blind}}: The victim cannot see, and is more likely to fail at attacking.
* {{st|Charmed}}: The victim becomes friendly to the one that charmed it.
* {{st|Exhaustion}}: A special debuff that increases in severity as it accumulates and is usually acquired by spending too long engaging in heavy activity without a chance for a reprieve.
* {{st|Fear}}: Resembles the "frightened" condition in that the victim no longer attempts to move closer to the source of its fear.
* {{st|Free Spell}}: Resembles a spell scroll, used to cast a spell without expending a spell slot.
* {{st|Grappled}}: The victim is {{st|Immobile|Immobilized}} until the grappler is dealt with. 
* {{st|Immobile}}: Resembles the "restrained" condition in that the victim can still fight, but cannot move.
* {{st|Petrify}}: The victim is transformed into a solid inanimate substance, such as a rock. They are incapacitated, unable to move, act, or defend themselves, but have increased resistance to all sources of damage.
* {{st|Stealth}}: Resembles the "invisible" condition. The unit is harder to attack.
* {{st|Stun}}: Resembles the "incapacitated" condition in that the victim cannot perform actions or reactions.

=== Other inspirations ===
* {{st|Doomed}}: Shares almost the same name as the [https://finalfantasy.fandom.com/wiki/Doom_(status) Doom] status from the Final Fantasy series. At the end of each turn, a timer counts down; when it reaches zero, the victim falls.
* The icons for {{st|Initiative Up}} and {{st|Initiative Down}} are based on the fable [[wikipedia:The Tortoise and the Hare|The Tortoise and the Hare]].
